newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Nov 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Nov 27.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Work in four wells of Kailashtila gas field in Sylhet district came to halt on the first day (Tuesday) of a three-day sit in strike by all-party action committee.

The leader of a six-member medical team now conducting a research in the arsenic polluted areas yesterday stressed the need for a joint move by the government and the NGOs to save public health from the danger.
Fertiliser production in the country faces a shortfall of 50,000 tonnes (against 21 lakh tonnes target) in fiscal 1996-97, according to official sources.
West Begal Chief Minister Jyoti Basu arrives here today to discuss with Bangladesh leaders bilateral issues including the crucial water sharing.

The President of Federation of Bangladesh Chambers of Commerce and Industry, Yusuf Abdullah Harun, has emphasised the need for consensus among major political parties on certain national issues for smooth economic growth of the country through investment and industrialisation.

Chairman of opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) Begum Khaleda Zia, leaving today for Saudi Arabia for treatment, has called for resisting attempts to rehabilitate the "fallen autocrat" and "conspiracies" to jeopardise the hard-earned democracy.
The authorities are contemplating strict compliance of regulations with regard to licensing new non-banking financial institutions in future.
Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) has delisted seven companies because of their failure to clear annual fees for the last few years.
